details:
Our project aims to transform the topographical structure of Mars’ Jezero Crater into a physical model that can assist in evaluating potential landing sites and safe surface routes for future Mars exploration missions.

Jezero Crater is a region of significant importance for understanding the surface characteristics of Mars and its geological history. However, assessing such an extensive and rugged terrain solely through two-dimensional maps or digital images can make it difficult to visualize elevation differences and terrain features. To address this challenge, we chose an alternative approach by creating a physical model of the crater.

During the development of our project, we first examined the actual topographical structure of Jezero Crater. Based on the crater’s geographical characteristics, elevation variations, and terrain features, we constructed a scale model that preserves the proportions of the original crater as accurately as possible. By emphasizing different elevations and surface formations within the model, we aimed to make the terrain easier to examine and interpret.

The primary purpose of our model is to support the assessment of potential astronaut landing sites and the planning of future exploration activities on the Martian surface. By physically examining different regions of the crater, we aim to evaluate how elevation changes, sloped areas, and terrain obstacles may affect potential landing and travel routes. This approach can help distinguish areas that may be more suitable for landing from those that require more careful assessment. Additionally, our model serves as a visual reference that can assist in identifying potential routes for astronauts and exploration vehicles to follow within the crater.

One of the main challenges we encountered during the development of our project was the limited technical experience and resources available within our team in the fields of software development and digital modeling. Therefore, rather than focusing exclusively on developing a digital platform, we decided to adopt a physical modeling approach. We also believed that a physical model would offer significant advantages by allowing direct observation of terrain features and easier comparison between different regions. In this way, we transformed our technical limitations into an alternative problem-solving approach.

One of the most important features of our project is its ability to transform complex topographical information into a tangible and understandable physical representation. In addition to making the Martian surface easier to examine, this model can contribute to the visualization of scientific data, the comparison of terrain characteristics, and a clearer understanding of potential mission plans.

Ultimately, as Team SCLASS, our goal is not simply to create a scale model of Jezero Crater, but to develop a practical and tangible tool that can help improve our understanding of the challenging surface conditions of Mars, support the evaluation of potential landing sites, and contribute to the planning of future human missions to Mars.
